## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.

package net.officefloor.hq.app.period;

import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest;
import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.time.YearMonth;
import java.util.List;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.Audit;
import net.officefloor.hq.app.sheet.Sheet;
import net.officefloor.plugin.variable.Out;
import net.officefloor.plugin.variable.Val;

/**
 * Makes one period per calendar month from the from-date's month to the to-date's month (a blank
 * from-date is the sheet's today), each running from the first to the last day of its month and
 * named yyyy-mm. A to-date before the from-date is refused. A month whose name is already a period,
 * or whose days overlap a period on the sheet, is left out; each made is saved and audited in turn.
 */
public class GeneratePeriods {
    public void generate(@Val GeneratePeriodsInput input, @Val Sheet sheet, PeriodRepository repository,
            HttpServletRequest request, Audit audit, Out<GeneratePeriodsResponse> result)
            throws InvalidPeriodException {
        LocalDate from = input.from() == null ? sheet.today() : input.from();
        if (input.to().isBefore(from)) {
            throw new InvalidPeriodException("A to-date is on or after the from-date");
        }
        result.set(new GeneratePeriodsResponse(months(from, input.to(), sheet, repository, request, audit)));
    }

    /** Makes and audits the monthly periods from the from-date's month to the to-date's month, as above: how many were made. */
    static int months(LocalDate from, LocalDate to, Sheet sheet, PeriodRepository repository,
            HttpServletRequest request, Audit audit) {
        List<Period> existing = repository.findAll(sheet.id());
        int made = 0;
        for (YearMonth month = YearMonth.from(from); !month.isAfter(YearMonth.from(to)); month = month.plusMonths(1)) {
            Period period = new Period(sheet.id(), month.toString(), month.atDay(1), month.atEndOfMonth());
            if (existing.stream().anyMatch(o -> o.name().equals(period.name()) || o.overlaps(period))) continue;
            repository.insert(period);
            audit.record("PERIOD_ADDED sheet=" + sheet.id() + " by=" + Audit.user(request)
                    + " period=" + period.name() + " from=" + period.from() + " to=" + period.to());
            made++;
        }
        return made;
    }
}

content.text:
I added the quarter generator, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**What it does:** a new "Year" box with a "Generate quarters" button in the Periods section. It creates the periods `<yyyy>-Q1` to `<yyyy>-Q4` for that calendar year (Jan–Mar, Apr–Jun, Jul–Sep, Oct–Dec). It shows how many were made in the same "Made N" count the monthly and fiscal-year generators already use.

- **Skipped quarters:** a quarter is left out if a period with its name already exists or its dates overlap another period. This is the same check the "Add period" form uses.
- **Saving:** each quarter that is made is saved and gets its own `PERIOD_ADDED` audit line.
- **Bad input:** anything other than a four-digit year is refused with the shared `period-generate-error` message, and nothing is written.

**Changes:**
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods/generate-quarters`, in `generate-quarters.POST.yml`. It is set up like the existing fiscal-year one, so viewers can't use it and a bad year is refused before anything is read or written. Behind it are four new classes in the `period` package: `GenerateQuarters`, `ValidateGenerateQuarters`, `GenerateQuartersRequest` and `QuarterYear`.
- **Front end:** the new form is in `features/periods/periods.slot.tsx`. It reuses the existing `period-generated` count and `period-generate-error` message.

There is no change to the stored data's schema: quarters are ordinary periods.
